about: What a settlement looks like to someone standing on its green or in its taproom: by its size, by the trade it lives by, and by where its inn and shrine stand. No census, and no etymology: those are for the journal.

hamlet: {name} is a handful of houses round a trodden green, with {trade}. Hens scratch in the dirt by the doors.
A few houses stand round a pound for strays at {name}, with {trade}. The air smells of dung and woodsmoke.
{name} is one farm grown into four, their yards running together, with {trade}. A cow lows somewhere behind a wall.
Three houses and a byre stand about a well at {name}, with {trade}. The well-chain knocks against the stones when the wind moves it.
{name} straggles along the track for a bowshot, house, garden, house, with {trade}. Smoke leans from the chimneys.
village: The houses of {name} stand round a wide green with their backs to the weather, with {trade}. Geese graze the grass short.
{name} is a green with a pond on it and houses round it, with {trade}. Ducks dabble at the pond's edge.
{name} is one long street with a green at the end of it, with {trade}. Cartwheels have cut the street into ruts that hold the water.
{name} climbs a slope from its green in steps of garden wall, with {trade}. A gate creaks somewhere, and a hammer rings.
At {name} the houses stand close round a green trodden bare, with {trade}. The smell of baking drifts from an open door.
{name} is built along a stream, with a plank bridge to every second door and {trade}. The water chatters under the planks.
town: Lanes run off {name} green between tall houses whose upper floors lean together overhead, with {trade} beyond. Carts rumble on the cobbles, and the air smells of smoke and horses.
{name} is a town of narrow lanes round a broad green, with {trade}. Bells, hammers and voices come from every side.
{name} has a market cross on its green and a wall round half of it, with {trade}. Pigeons strut on the cross's worn steps.
{name} is a town of two streets crossing at a green, with {trade}. A smith's hammer rings from one corner, and the smell of a bakehouse comes from another.
Carts stand about {name} green, the horses steaming in the shafts, with {trade} beyond. The lanes off it are loud with hammering and the cries of hawkers.

trade.salt: salt-houses black with tar along the shore
trade.reed: reed drying in ricks behind the houses
trade.tin: spoil heaps grey above the roofs
trade.iron: red smoke from the bloomery hearths and red dust on every sill
trade.timber: timber stacked to season by the road
trade.charcoal: the blue smoke of charcoal hearths beyond the houses
trade.honey: bee-skeps in rows along the garden walls
trade.furs: pelts stretched on frames by the doors
trade.whale oil: the reek of the try-pots down by the shore

inn: The sign of {inn} creaks over its door, and across the green the shrine of {cult} stands open.
{inn} faces the shrine of {cult} across the green.
{inn} stands at a corner of the green with its door propped open; the shrine of {cult} is along from it.
Next to {inn} is the shrine of {cult}, so close that the inn's smoke goes over its roof.
The shrine of {cult} stands at the head of the green, and {inn} faces it across the grass.

hamlet: A low room with a peat fire, one long table and a bench along the wall, all of it smelling of smoke.
The inn is one room, with the fire at one end, the barrels at the other and a long table scarred with knife-marks between them.
The inn is a kitchen with a long table and a counter in it. A pot of something with onions in it simmers on the hearth.
village: A low-beamed room, dark with old smoke, where the fire spits under a black kettle and the benches are polished with sitting.
A smoky room under low beams, with a settle by the fire and a dog asleep under it. The rushes on the floor smell of ale and wet boots.
A long low room, whitewashed, with a fire at the far end whose warmth reaches only halfway. Pewter mugs hang in a row on hooks above the counter.
town: A long room with a fire at either end and talk going on all down it, under hams hung from the beams. The boards are tacky with spilled ale.
A busy room in two parts with a counter between them, and a stair going up to the bedrooms. It smells of roasting meat, and the clatter of the kitchen comes through the back door.
A high room hung with nets and lanterns, crowded and loud. Smoke from the hearth gathers under the roof-beams, and a song starts up in a corner and dies.

drinkers.salt: Salt-boilers sit at the long table, still white to the elbow.
drinkers.eels: Eel-men sit at the long table, smelling of the river.
drinkers.reed: Reed-cutters sit at the long table, their hands cut and bound.
drinkers.tin: Miners sit at the long table, grey with dust to the eyebrows.
drinkers.iron: Ironmen sit at the long table, red to the wrist with the ore.
drinkers.wool: Shepherds sit at the long table, with their dogs asleep under it.
drinkers.timber: Woodmen sit at the long table, sawdust in their hair.
drinkers.charcoal: Colliers sit at the long table, black to the elbow.
drinkers.honey: A beekeeper sits at the long table, her veil in her lap.
drinkers.slate: Quarrymen sit at the long table, grey-handed, talking low.
drinkers.furs: Trappers sit at the long table, quiet over their beer.
drinkers.whale oil: Men from the try-works sit at the long table, and the reek of the pots has come in with them.
drinkers.peat: Peat-cutters sit at the long table, their boots still black.

life.salt: Someone is raking out a salt-pan at the end of the green, and the steam comes off it white.
life.eels: Two women are skinning eels on a bench by the water, and the cats are watching.
life.reed: A man goes by with a bundle of reed on his back as big as himself.
life.tin: A string of ponies goes through with panniers of grey ore, heads down.
life.iron: A cart of red ore grinds through toward the hearths, and the road behind it is rust-coloured.
life.wool: Sheep are being driven through, bleating, and the way fills with the smell of wet fleece.
life.timber: Somebody is splitting logs behind the houses, and the sound comes back off the walls.
life.charcoal: A cart goes by loaded with charcoal sacks, and black dust sifts from it onto the road.
life.honey: A child is selling honey-cake from a tray, waving the wasps off it.
life.slate: The tap of slate-splitters comes from a yard behind the houses, steady as rain.
life.furs: A trapper is haggling at a door with a bundle of pelts over one shoulder.
life.whale oil: Gulls scream and fight over something on the shore.
life.peat: A sledge of turves goes by, pulled by a man and a shaggy pony, both bent to the weight.
